traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 883 records annotated as flowering (Jan 2, Feb 9, Mar 164, Apr 625, May 77, Jun 5, Jul 1); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, March and April. FEIS (Rubus spectabilis) gives March to June for western Oregon and southwestern Washington.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA National Phenology Network observations (Nature's Notebook) at lowland sites west of the Cascades in Washington and Oregon (below 300 m, west of 121.8° W; 2009 to 2026, fetched 2026-10-14): 34 plant-years at 14 sites seen with ripe fruit, by the months they were seen in (Feb 1, Apr 2, May 10, Jun 16, Jul 12, Aug 4, Sep 1); stated as the months with at least a third as many as the busiest, May to July. FEIS (Rubus spectabilis): ripe from May to July at Bella Coola, British Columbia; generally June and July in the south of its range.

traits.height_max_m.note: Jepson (1925), as R. spectabilis: grows 91 cm to 2.74 m tall (converted from feet).

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a thicket of tall, upright to arching, golden-brown stems with leaves of three toothed leaflets and single magenta flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 2.2 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green leaflets; magenta flowers; shredding golden-brown bark. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: the last salmonberries, raspberry-like, yellow-orange to red, about 2 cm long. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: magenta flowers in March to May; berries yellow-orange to red in late May into July. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): golden-brown bark shredding and peeling; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five magenta petals between five sepals on a floral cup and about ninety stamens round its pistils, from the characters of its own, Rosaceae's and Rubus's by the rules at the flowering plants.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.note: The Burke Herbarium's account of the species, as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read: stamens 75 to 100; pistils numerous; petals pink to purplish red.

traits.flowering_position.note: FEIS's salmonberry review (page read): the flowers are borne on short, leafy lateral stalks.
